Contract or expected behavior: 201, Location, StudentResponse (createStudent responses).
Actual behavior: 200; no Location; only id and message.
Steps to reproduce: Contract Tests > Create student: POST a valid name, major, gpa and birth date.
Severity: Major. Generated clients cannot deserialize the promised resource or follow Location.

Contract or expected behavior: 200 with full StudentResponse (updateStudent).
Actual behavior: Only a message is returned.
Steps to reproduce: Create student; PUT valid replacement details to its returned id.
Severity: Major. The documented update response cannot be consumed as StudentResponse.

Contract or expected behavior: dateOfBirth is writeOnly and never returned (StudentRequest.dateOfBirth).
Actual behavior: Reads expose dateOfBirth; CSV contains its column and stored value.
Steps to reproduce: D12: create student with 2004-01-06; GET by id, filter by unique major, GET export.
Severity: Critical. Protected student data is disclosed, including by an undocumented export endpoint.

Contract or expected behavior: CourseResponse requires instructorId integer.
Actual behavior: Returns instructor instead of instructorId.
Steps to reproduce: Create course with instructor 11; GET by id and list; PUT valid details.
Severity: Major. Required field is missing from every normal course representation.

Contract or expected behavior: roster contains StudentSummary objects with id and name; one entry per student.
Actual behavior: roster is a set of name strings. Two students named Same Name collapse to one displayed entry.
Steps to reproduce: D10: create two distinct students with same name; enroll both in one course; GET course and enrollment count.
Severity: Major. Roster loses identity and hides enrolled students with duplicate names.

Contract or expected behavior: CourseResponse.status enum is OPEN or CLOSED.
Actual behavior: A full course returns FULL.
Steps to reproduce: Create a capacity-one course with one initial student; GET it (Full course status uses documented enum).
Severity: Major. A legitimate full course breaks enum-based clients.

Contract or expected behavior: Only courses taught by requested instructor (listCourses query description).
Actual behavior: Courses for instructor 22 are included too.
Steps to reproduce: Create instructor-11 and instructor-22 courses; query instructorId=11; compare returned ids.
Severity: Major. Clients receive unrelated courses when filtering.

Contract or expected behavior: 200 JSON CourseResponse (addStudentToCourse).
Actual behavior: 200 text/plain success message.
Steps to reproduce: Create student and course; PUT the student id as a bare JSON number.
Severity: Major. Successful enrollment has an incompatible response format.

Contract or expected behavior: 404 ErrorResponse for missing course/student.
Actual behavior: 400 text/plain No such course exists.
Steps to reproduce: Create student; PUT its id to addStudent/-1 (Missing add course).
Severity: Major. Clients cannot distinguish missing resources using documented status and body.

Contract or expected behavior: 404 ErrorResponse if student is absent.
Actual behavior: 200 student-shaped object containing null fields and empty courses.
Steps to reproduce: GET /api/students/-1 (Missing student).
Severity: Major. An absent student is falsely reported as a successful resource lookup.

Contract or expected behavior: 400 uses ErrorResponse with timestamp, status, error, message, path.
Actual behavior: 400 contains only field-name validation messages.
Steps to reproduce: POST {}; create valid student then PUT {} to its id.
Severity: Major. Common validation errors break the shared error parser.

Contract or expected behavior: 204 on success; 404 ErrorResponse for missing id.
Actual behavior: 200 on successful deletion; empty body and no JSON type for missing id.
Steps to reproduce: Create unenrolled student; DELETE it; separately DELETE /api/students/-1.
Severity: Minor. Deletion works for unlinked students, but status/error representation differs.

Contract or expected behavior: 200 array of CourseResponse; 404 for absent student.
Actual behavior: 501 Not Implemented for both existing and absent ids.
Steps to reproduce: Create and enroll student; GET its courses; repeat with -1.
Severity: Major. The entire documented operation is unavailable.

Contract or expected behavior: Accepts RosterChangeRequest object containing studentId.
Actual behavior: Documented object returns 400 before business logic; bare number works.
Steps to reproduce: D01: enroll a student; PUT {studentId: saved id}; then diagnostic bare-number request. D23 covers nonmember.
Severity: Major. A client following the request schema cannot remove any enrollment.

Contract or expected behavior: 404 ErrorResponse for an absent course.
Actual behavior: 400 with JSON number -1.
Steps to reproduce: GET /api/courses/getEnrollment/-1.
Severity: Major. The documented error status and body type are both incompatible.

Contract or expected behavior: 400 for validation errors, oversized initial roster or capacity below existing roster.
Actual behavior: 500 ErrorResponse instead; rejected updates preserve stored data.
Steps to reproduce: POST course with empty name; PUT maxSize 0. D21 shrinks below roster. D22 creates initial roster over capacity.
Severity: Major. Ordinary client errors become server failures; clients may retry invalid writes.

Contract or expected behavior: 404 when roster contains a nonexistent student (createCourse/updateCourse).
Actual behavior: Unknown ids are silently ignored. Updating to roster [-1] returns 200 and erases valid enrollment.
Steps to reproduce: D24: enroll valid student; PUT valid course details with roster [-1]; read course and student. D18 covers creation.
Severity: Critical. Invalid input silently destroys an existing relationship while reporting success.

Contract or expected behavior: 409 for already-enrolled student; count equals current roster size.
Actual behavior: Duplicate returns 200; roster stays one while enrollment count becomes two.
Steps to reproduce: D02: create student and course; enroll same id twice; GET course, student and enrollment.
Severity: Major. Repeated calls corrupt enrollment reporting.

Contract or expected behavior: 409 when course is full (addStudentToCourse).
Actual behavior: 500 for second distinct student at capacity one. Persisted roster/count remain one.
Steps to reproduce: D03: create two students and capacity-one course; enroll first; attempt second; read all three views.
Severity: Major. Full-course transition fails as a server error; no persisted over-enrollment was observed.

Contract or expected behavior: Enrollment count is number currently on roster (getCourseEnrollment description).
Actual behavior: Initial and replacement roster show one student, but count remains zero.
Steps to reproduce: D04: create course with initial student. D05: create empty course then PUT roster containing student. Read roster, student and count.
Severity: Major. Different write paths produce inconsistent reporting.

Contract or expected behavior: courses creates/replaces enrollments (createStudent/updateStudent and StudentRequest.courses).
Actual behavior: Create loses requested enrollment; update leaves old course and fails to add new course.
Steps to reproduce: D06: create course then student with courses [id]. D07: enroll in A, update student to [B], read student, both courses and counts.
Severity: Major. Enrollment writes report success without applying the requested relationships.

Contract or expected behavior: Deletes student and removes them from every roster (deleteStudent description).
Actual behavior: 500; student remains and course still contains the student; count stays one.
Steps to reproduce: D08: create student/course, enroll, DELETE student; GET student, course and count.
Severity: Major. Enrolled students cannot be deleted through the promised lifecycle operation.

Contract or expected behavior: StudentResponse.courses has one entry per course.
Actual behavior: Two distinct enrolled courses with same name collapse to one displayed entry.
Steps to reproduce: D11: create two courses named Same Course; enroll same student in both; read student and both rosters.
Severity: Major. Student view silently omits one distinct enrollment.

Contract or expected behavior: StudentRequest.name maxLength 100; invalid input returns 400.
Actual behavior: 101-character name accepted with 200 and a generated id.
Steps to reproduce: D14: submit names of length 99, 100 and 101; compare acceptance.
Severity: Minor. The documented input maximum is not enforced.

Contract or expected behavior: StudentRequest.required includes gpa; missing field returns 400.
Actual behavior: Missing GPA accepted with 200 and a generated id.
Steps to reproduce: D16: POST valid name and major without gpa.
Severity: Major. Required academic data can be absent.
